title: Feelings Faces Game
description: For ages 6–9 with an adult: draw and mime feelings for others to guess, and talk about what each feeling is like.

body.heading: Draw the faces
paragraphs: Draw simple faces on pieces of paper — happy, sad, surprised, worried, excited, sleepy, cross. Big eyes and mouths make the feelings easy to see.
Look in the mirror and copy each face. Feel how your eyebrows, eyes, and mouth all move together to make one feeling.

body.heading: Mime and guess
paragraphs: Shuffle the cards. Take one, look at it secretly, and make that face. Everyone else guesses which feeling you are showing.
Some faces are easy to guess. Some are tricky — a worried face and a thinking face can look almost the same.

body.heading: Feelings are messages
paragraphs: Feelings tell us what we need. A sad friend might need company. A cross friend might need space and quiet.
When you can read faces, you can be kind at the right moment, in the right way.

takeaway: Faces show feelings like signs, and learning to read them helps you know how to be kind.
safetyNotes: Every feeling is allowed in this game — there are no wrong feelings, only guesses about faces.
screenFreeExtension: Notice feelings on faces around you today and think about what each person might need.
